cards.title: 717 claimed ransomware victims in November 2025
cards.description: Bitdefender Labs recorded 717 organizations claimed by ransomware groups on Data Leak Sites between November 1 and November 30, 2025. The figure aggregates self-reported victim postings across all tracked RaaS operations and reflects continued high-volume extortion activity heading into year-end.

cards.title: Qilin claimed 122 victims, down from 205
cards.description: After running its August-to-October Korean Leaks campaign against an MSP ecosystem, Qilin's claimed victim count fell to 122 in November 2025 — a sharp drop from 205 the previous month. The sparkline contrasts the October peak with the post-campaign November cool-off, while Qilin still held the #1 position in Bitdefender's Top 10.

cards.title: Qilin victim count: October vs November 2025
cards.description: Qilin's monthly claimed-victim count fell from 205 in October 2025 to 122 in November 2025 — roughly a 40% month-over-month decline — as the group's Korean Leaks MSP campaign wound down. Bitdefender retains Qilin at the #1 position in its Top 10 ransomware families despite the drop.

cards.title: Clop claimed 102 victims, reclaiming the Top 10
cards.description: Clop posted 102 victims in November 2025, surpassing Akira to retake the #2 position in Bitdefender's Top 10. The group concentrated on manufacturing, technology and healthcare targets, repeatedly leveraging a zero-day affecting Oracle E-Business Suite (CVE-2025-61882) to compromise large numbers of systems.

cards.title: Top ransomware families by claimed victims, Nov 2025
cards.description: Among Bitdefender's Top 10, Qilin again led with 122 claimed victims in November 2025, followed by Clop with 102. Clop's rise was driven by exploitation of an Oracle E-Business Suite zero-day, pushing Akira out of the #2 slot. The two leading groups alone accounted for roughly 31% of the 717 total claimed victims for the month.

cards.title: Warlock claimed 3 Russia-based victims in one month
cards.description: Warlock listed 3 victims based in Russia during November 2025 — a highly unusual event given most Russian-aligned actors avoid domestic targets. Bitdefender notes shared TTPs with state-sponsored Storm-2603 (which abused SharePoint ToolShell flaws) and reads the incident as supporting evidence that Warlock is a China-based operation.

cards.title: Traditional RaaS profit margin: 85–90% for operators
cards.description: Bitdefender researchers observe that the typical Ransomware-as-a-Service split leaves 85–90% of paid ransoms with operators (or affiliates, depending on the model). Kryptos' new insider-recruitment scheme is explicitly designed to expand profit-sharing beyond this baseline by paying corporate insiders for VPN, MFA and SSH access.

cards.title: Insider payoff range
cards.description: Bitdefender describes Kryptos' tiered profit-sharing scheme for corporate insiders — IT admins, executive assistants and third-party vendors — who hand over VPN, MFA or SSH access. Removing the need for EDR/AV-killers and infostealers, the model rewards insiders with payments scaled to the value of access provided.
cards.quote: "The payoff for those willing to become an insider threat runs from thousands of dollars all the way up to millions of dollars."

cards.title: 7 RaaS brands in a single alleged alliance
cards.description: Stormous announced version 5 of its RaaS in October 2025 along with a strategic partnership purportedly tying together seven groups: Stormous, Devman, Coinbase Cartel, Nova, Radar, Desolator and Kryptos. Researchers questioned the legitimacy of the alliance citing operational-model clashes and a lack of corroborating communication from named partners.

cards.title: React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) hits 4 React versions
cards.description: CVE-2025-55182 is a critical flaw in React Server Components that enables initial access and remote code execution via crafted HTTP requests containing malicious objects. React 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1 and 19.2.0 are affected, alongside default Next.js 15.x and 16.x configurations and 14.x Canary builds. Bitdefender warns the impact may rival Log4Shell.

cards.title: Clop exploits Oracle EBS zero-day CVE-2025-61882
cards.description: Clop's November 2025 campaign repeatedly weaponised CVE-2025-61882, a flaw enabling compromise of Oracle Concurrent Processing in Oracle E-Business Suite versions 12.2.14 through 12.2.3. Organisations running affected EBS versions are urged to apply the vendor patch to disrupt the group's mass-exploitation pipeline.

cards.title: Clop's primary target industries, Nov 2025
cards.description: Of Clop's 102 claimed victims in November 2025, Bitdefender flags manufacturing, technology and healthcare as the dominant verticals — sectors aligned with the group's Oracle E-Business Suite exploitation strategy. The chart illustrates the named priority targets called out in the debrief; exact per-industry counts are not enumerated in the source text.

cards.title: Akira: ~1 year targeting Nutanix VMs
cards.description: CISA's updated Akira advisory underscores that the group has been targeting Nutanix VMs for nearly a year. Akira's Linux encryptor in the Nutanix AHV environment encrypts virtual disks (`.qcow2`) without first powering down VMs — a divergence from the standard ESXi attack flow.

cards.title: Nova RaaS exposed by CBSecurity leak
cards.description: In early December 2025 a group calling itself CBSecurity dumped Nova ransomware staff names, roles and infrastructure IPs. Bitdefender assesses the leak was likely engineered by an angry affiliate or competitor reacting to Nova's targeting of education and non-profit victims earlier in the year.
cards.quote: "A group named CBSecurity leaked the names and roles associated with Nova staff and multiple IP addresses tied to their infrastructure."

cards.title: ShinySp1d3r Windows encryptor capabilities
cards.description: ShinyHunters' newly released ShinySp1d3r RaaS bundles a Windows encryptor capable of suppressing Event Viewer logging, force-killing processes, and deploying malware via SCM and WMI. Bitdefender suggests this in-house tooling — released just before Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters' August takedown — may become a template for other groups breaking away from third-party affiliates.
cards.quote: "The encryptor's ability to hook EtwEventWrite to offset the writing of data into Windows Event Viewer, its ability to force kill open processes, and also run malware locally via actions such as deployViaSCM and deployViaWMI."

cards.title: Korean Leaks: 30+ South Korean orgs breached
cards.description: From August through October 2025, Qilin — working with a partner likely linked to Moonstone Sleet — leveraged a compromised MSP ecosystem to leak data from more than 30 South Korea-based organisations. Bitdefender ties this campaign directly to Qilin's October peak of 205 victims and its sharp November fall-off to 122.

cards.title: Bitdefender Labs sees 400+ new threats per minute
cards.description: Bitdefender Labs reports discovering more than 400 new threats every minute and validating 30 billion threat queries each day across its telemetry. With more than 180 technology brands embedding Bitdefender's stack via OEM partnerships, the vendor positions this dataset as one of the industry's broadest real-time threat-landscape feeds.

cards.title: 30 billion threat queries validated daily
cards.description: Bitdefender's global telemetry validates 30 billion threat queries per day across hundreds of millions of endpoints. The scale underpins the visibility behind monthly debriefs and contextualises the 717-victim ransomware tally observed in November 2025.

cards.title: 180+ technology brands embed Bitdefender
cards.description: Bitdefender notes more than 180 third-party technology vendors license its detection and protection engines through OEM agreements. The OEM footprint amplifies the company's visibility into the threat landscape beyond its own first-party consumer and business products.

cards.title: Ransomware claimed-victim mix — Qilin & Clop share of 717
cards.description: Qilin (122) and Clop (102) together accounted for 224 of November 2025's 717 claimed ransomware victims — roughly 31% of the total — with the remaining 493 victims distributed across the rest of the tracked Top 10 and long tail of smaller RaaS operations.

cards.title: Frameworks impacted by React2Shell
cards.description: CVE-2025-55182 affects four React releases (19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1, 19.2.0), the default configurations of Next.js 15.x and 16.x, and Canary builds of Next.js 14.x. This chart illustrates the affected-component footprint Bitdefender flags as a potential Log4Shell-style mass-exploitation risk.
